objective: Prove, for the hub-free parity laws of OPEN-END-GROWTH-20261107-001B and the two-kind spheres of GROW-COIN-20261107-001A, with K1-K3 checked by computation (knotlab relations): (1) for a fixed substrate the joint law of a growth history and the world's states is a product when the rule reads only the law, so no knot joins the order to the states, and a history meets the world's knots only through existence, as the presence literal of the canonical test; (2) the local history (which neighbour came first) is a 2-CNF relation and so holds no knot, while time without cycles is one not-all-equal knot per cycle of the world, so on a ring the beginning is a knot binding every seam, and it contradicts the local history there; (3) Euler's count: under any local history the world's Euler characteristic equals its beginnings minus its closing moves plus its ends, so growth without closing moves builds only trees, discs and spheres; (4) no radius-r law with k hidden labels that allows a long enough thread excludes every ring (pumping), while the open-end rule grows threads and never rings, so a beginning does work no bounded static witness does in one dimension; in two dimensions a law excludes flat tori exactly when its flat configurations are aperiodic. Check every finite claim by computation with controls that fail.
status: Proved 2026-11-07: for growth rules that read only the law, the order never knots with the world's states (a product on each fixed world; when worlds vary every knot with an order variable contains an existence variable, and existence enters as a presence literal); the local history (at most one parent) is 2-CNF with no knot, while the knots of time without a loop are exactly the world's cycles, so on a ring the beginning is one NAE knot over every seam; Euler's count makes sprouting build only trees and disc moves only discs and spheres; a radius-r law with k hidden labels that allows a thread of (2r+1)k^(2r+1) + 2r + 3 knots allows a ring, so a beginning does in one dimension what no bounded witness does, and in two only an aperiodic law excludes flat tori (the seam law allows every one).
title: A beginning is a knot: a growth history under the knot test
